topic.title: Education: Origins and daily operation in Community Learning Centres
topic.focus: how the initiative began and how it works each day

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-25. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: An accident of tenancy
sections.text: The account Ogniwo gives of itself is a pedagogical one. In 1999, when the training department of the Sendzimir steelworks in Nowa Huta was wound up, two of its instructors, Halina Wrona and Tadeusz Bielak, resolved to carry on teaching the workers whom the closure had left mid-course. The association's minute books, deposited with the Kraków city archive in 2018, tell a less purposeful story. What they record for the winter of 1999–2000 is not a curriculum but a search for a room: Wrona and Bielak taught in a scout hut, in the back room of a pharmacy on aleja Róż, and for one term in a corridor. Even the name was not chosen. Ogniwo — 'a link in a chain' — was already painted on the door of the cellar in Osiedle Szkolne that the housing cooperative let them use from October 2000 at a rent of one złoty a year, and it stuck. Not until 2005, when registration as an association became a condition of applying for municipal money, did anyone set down in writing what the centre was for.

sections.heading: The Wednesday allocation
sections.text: Twenty-six years later Ogniwo teaches in two premises in the district, but its daily operation still turns on a procedure improvised in that cellar. The centre does not run terms, and it publishes no timetable more than eight days ahead. Tutors meet instead on Wednesday evenings to allocate the following week's sessions against a handwritten ledger, known to everyone as the hour bank, in which each tutor's availability and each learner's outstanding request is entered by hand. Three strands are taught: Polish for speakers of other languages, basic numeracy, and a course on the state's online services, ePUAP and mObywatel, added in 2016 when applications for child benefit moved onto the internet. A session lasts ninety minutes and a learner may book four a week. Anyone who arrives without a booking is admitted if a chair is free; the centre logged 63 such admissions in March 2025 alone, which suggests that a chair usually is.

sections.heading: Two explanations, one set of figures
sections.text: Whether any of this explains the centre's results is contested. In 2019 a team from the Jagiellonian University's Institute of Education compared Ogniwo with four municipal adult centres in Kraków and found its learners markedly less likely to abandon a course: 58 per cent completed, against a municipal average of 41 per cent. The report attributed the difference to the eight-day timetable, which let learners on rotating shifts arrange study around their work rather than the reverse. A re-analysis commissioned by the city's education department in 2022 accepted the figures and rejected the explanation. Both Ogniwo premises, it observed, stand within 400 metres of a tram stop, whereas three of the four comparison centres do not; once journey time was controlled for, the advantage narrowed to six percentage points, and what remained lay within the margin the sample could support. Neither team disputed that something at Ogniwo works. They disagreed about whether it was the pedagogy or the pavement.

sections.heading: What the accounts do not settle
sections.text: Ogniwo's own figures call for similar caution. The association spent 1,240,000 złoty in 2023, of which 768,800 złoty went on salaries for four part-time coordinators and some two dozen hourly-paid tutors, and it recorded 612 enrolments — a little over 2,000 złoty an enrolment, which is the figure quoted in its funding applications. That figure is not a cost per person. A learner who takes both numeracy and ePUAP is counted twice, so the 612 enrolments correspond to 470 individuals, and the cost per individual is nearer 2,638 złoty. Wrona has never concealed the distinction, but the smaller number is the one that funders set beside municipal provision, and the centre has an evident interest in quoting it. A second ambiguity has attracted less attention: Ogniwo counts a learner as completing a course once two-thirds of booked sessions have been attended, a threshold the municipal centres do not apply, and neither the 2019 study nor the 2022 re-analysis examined it.

sections.heading: Everything that is not written down
sections.text: The vulnerability of the model is archival rather than financial. The Wednesday allocation works because Wrona, now 71, knows which tutor can be asked to take a Saturday at short notice and which learner will stop coming if moved to an unfamiliar room. In 2024 a volunteer developer offered to replace the ledger with scheduling software. The pilot ran for eleven weeks and was then abandoned — not because it failed to produce a timetable, but because it produced one that nobody was willing to defend. The ledger, it emerged, had been recording judgements as well as hours. The association has since agreed to appoint a second coordinator to sit in on the Wednesday meeting for a year before Wrona retires, a decision that concedes precisely the point the software exposed: most of what Ogniwo knows about its learners exists in the heads of the people who are closest to leaving.
